comment: The vectors pinning the runtime role's settings and the release's log settings, every name the Go runtime role will parse (the native Locus plan, §15.1): until then Locus.Config reads them (Locus.Config.from_env/2, with Locus.Runtime.Settings.pool/2 for the pool's), and apps/locus/test/locus/runtime/settings_test.exs holds it to every case; the core's roster test (apps/cyfr/test/cyfr/platform_settings_roster_test.exs) reads the names here where it declared Locus.Config's, and Locus.Config's own stay the builds', the backends' and a runner's. variables are the names in Locus.Config's order, the runtime role's and then the release's log settings: each its setting, what it accepts (a list is every value the setting takes, a sentence what the boot's refusal says it takes), and its default when unset, null for one that is required (required: the runtime's key, without which the node serves no runtime, and the host API's URL). A whole number carries the range it is read in (min and max, each inclusive) and the most characters it is read in (max_length, a sign among them). The host API's URL is read by the grammar worker_api.json's base_urls hold (grammar, Prima.WorkerWire.base_url/1), and the bind as a pin's ip is read (Prima.PinnedTarget.parse_ip/1), which host_api.json's pin cases hold: four decimal IPv4 fields, none with a leading zero or a sign, and a zone after an IPv6 address its own text. The attach directory's default is the run folder KEEPER_RUN_DIR names (default_from), and default where that names none or an empty one; KEEPER_RUN_DIR is read as written, not trimmed, and refused as the attach directory is. environment is the environment every case starts from, and the runtime's key in it is a fixture's. reads are environments each read as its settings, every one of them (the key as its hexadecimal text, the bind as written, the port and the durations as integers, the log's level and format as their names); refusals are environments each refused with its message, each for one cause: a boot with two causes is refused naming one of them. A setting's value is read with the white space around it trimmed, Unicode's white space, and a value of white space alone is unset; that holds for the settings, not for a name the release must not see (a control-plane name, or a LOCUS_ name no role reads), which refuses the boot whatever its value, empty or white space alone among them. No message shows the key.
